exposure: intravenous analgesic pump with esketamine and Sufentanil
cohort: The study included 147 women who underwent cesarean deliveries at Xiamen Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine between April 2022 and May 2024, divided into an observation group (n=81) receiving esketamine-based analgesia and a control group (n=66) receiving standard pain management.
finding: Esketamine-based postoperative analgesia for cesarean section significantly reduced perioperative pain, lowered postpartum depression scores at 3 and 7 days, mitigated inflammatory and stress responses, and showed neuroprotective effects without increasing adverse reactions compared to the control group.
